crime: In the lounge, a girl asked {WITCH_NAME} to come along to the recreation room. {WITCH_NAME} looked to the girl at her side; the girl answered for her that {WITCH_NAME} would stay, and she did. The other girls began bringing their questions to the girl at her side.

A night lamp sat in its bracket high on the wall of the cell corridor; each evening one of the girls lit it, and before the steps whoever lit it had to be lifted to reach the glass. Weeks before, {WITCH_NAME} had set a tall set of steps beneath the lamp — holding a piece in mind cost her nothing, and she never said they were hers. The girls went up them each evening to light it.

That evening in the lounge, a girl said {WITCH_NAME} should light the lamp since she had never done it before. The girl at {WITCH_NAME}'s side answered for her that {WITCH_NAME} would rather not climb up and that she herself would light it. {WITCH_NAME} said nothing.

At the lamp hour, the girl stood at the top of the steps, the wick lit and the glass settling back over it, with both hands flat on the smooth glass at full stretch. {WITCH_NAME} stood at the far end of the corridor, watching. She let the steps go.

The footing gone from under the girl, hands sliding from the smooth glass — backward and down the height of the steps onto the corridor stone, head first. The girl was found dead under the lamp, nothing standing beneath it.
At the trial, no girl had made the steps. None had carried them in, and none could say where they had come from; each had taken them for another girl's doing.

The girls in the nearby cells saw the corridor each night, and {WITCH_NAME}'s cellmate knew when {WITCH_NAME} went to bed. Week after week, the steps stood under the lamp on nights when {WITCH_NAME} stayed up and were gone on nights when she turned in early. Whatever she creates lasts only while she is awake; sleep unmakes it.
Only the mind that set the steps could take them away. Two girls coming down to the cells reached the corridor at the sound of the fall and saw {WITCH_NAME} standing at its end.
fields.epitaph: The only home that ever answered her held only as long as she could hold it.
fields.epithet: She Who Furnished the Absent House
execution: A bare iron bed frame occupied the middle of the stand. Iron points stood up out of the floor, from under the frame to the edges of the stand.
She was brought in between the points to the frame — iron stood on every side.
She set a bed board in the empty frame, from the home she imagines, and lay down on it. Only the board kept her back from the points beneath.
Before morning she fell asleep, and the board was gone. She fell onto the points below, her back and the back of her head first. They went in under her weight and killed her.

magic.name: House of Air
magic.text: She can bring things from the home she imagines into reality.
